professionalBackground.title: Professional Background
paragraphs: Daniel Cohen holds an M.A. in Statistics & Applied Mathematics (Hunter College, GPA 3.93), an MBA in Finance & Investments (Baruch College — Zicklin, Finance GPA 4.00), and a B.A. in Mathematics & Economics (Queens College — Magna Cum Laude). Society of Actuaries exams P/1, FM/2, and MFE ground his work in probability, financial mathematics, and risk thinking.

Paid work history spans more than a decade of college and K–12 mathematics instruction — Business Statistics labs with Excel, grading and scoring against answer keys, partial-credit decisions, written feedback, electronic grade and attendance records, progress reporting, and remote college teaching by Zoom — plus earlier bookkeeping and bank-reconciliation work at Village Copier. These roles built accuracy, clear communication, and independent responsibility.

analyticsAiTransition.title: Independent Technical Projects
paragraphs: Alongside that employment history, Daniel built a body of independent technical work. The Daniel AI Suite — seven deployed Streamlit applications plus SQL/Excel workbooks — applies statistical modeling, simulation, optimization, and testing to problems in finance, sports, music, and decision support.

In these projects he designs the analysis, implements it in Python, SQL, and Excel, checks results for accuracy, tests expected against actual behavior, diagnoses defects, and iterates, using AI-assisted tooling that he directs and verifies personally. This is independent project work and practice, not prior corporate analytics, AI-evaluation, or software-engineering employment.
Together — documented employment in teaching, scoring, records, and Excel, and demonstrated technical capability — these support part-time, contract, and project-based analytical assignments.

My training — an M.A. in Statistics & Applied Mathematics, an MBA in Finance, and three SOA exams — is applied in seven independent projects: live applications and workbooks that use statistical modeling, simulation, optimization, and testing.

My employment history is in teaching and earlier bookkeeping: more than a decade of grading and scoring, maintaining electronic records, working in Excel, giving written feedback, teaching remotely, and meeting deadlines independently. Those jobs built the same habits good analytical work needs — accuracy, clear explanation, and reliability.
I am open to remote part-time, contract, project-based, and flexible analytical work — data analysis, Excel and SQL, records and scoring review, and quantitative or mathematical review.
